correctness.rationale: For compact interior support, the generator identity is valid for the required smooth test functions. On \(\alpha+\beta=2\), invariance of \(\log(x+y+z)\) and \(x+y+z\) forces \(x+y+z=1\) almost surely. The coordinate generator identity then gives zero conditional mean per-capita growth; on the simplex this is \((\alpha-1)(z-y)\) for the first coordinate and cyclic analogues. Since \(\alpha\ne1\), the conditional equal-sharing laws follow. Their first- and second-moment consequences give equal means, equal variances, covariance \(-\sigma^2/2\), and correlation \(-1/2\) whenever \(\sigma^2>0\). The zero-variance case is exactly the coexistence Dirac mass. A symbolic checker independently verifies the two algebraic simplifications; no finite experiment is used as proof.

value.rationale: The parameter line \(\alpha+\beta=2\) is not an arbitrary slice: it is the classical integrable/periodic transition singled out in the May–Leonard literature. The conditional law is stronger than a global mean balance and yields a parameter- and orbit-independent statistical fingerprint: every non-equilibrium compact interior stationary state has pairwise correlation exactly \(-1/2\). This supplies an exact diagnostic for critical coexistence cycles and a reusable invariant for analytic or computational studies. The result is self-contained and excludes the degenerate \(\alpha=1\) case where the conclusion is false.
